newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PC and phone boom boosts profit at NEC.
newsitem.headline: Japan PC and phone boom boosts profit at NEC.

text.p: NEC Corp reported a strong rise in annual profits Thursday as Japan's booming market for mobile phones and communications gadgets burnished its balance sheet.
The Japanese electronics giant said its group net profit rose 18 percent in the fiscal year ended March 31 to 91.58 billion yen ($789 million).
Group sales rose 12.5 percent to 4.9 trillion yen ($42.2 billion) amid a surge in demand for mobile communications equipment and PCs in the domestic market.
"A decline in our overseas sales was more than offset by a big increase in sales in domestic mobile communications and personal computer markets," NEC said in a statement.
Mobile phones have become a standard fashion accessory in Japan, especially for teenagers, and PC sales have been buoyant as the country has belatedly caught the Internet bug.

Group pre-tax profit slipped 19.9 percent to 121.2 billion yen ($1.04 billion) in the year, mainly due to a sharp decline in chip prices that started at the beginning of 1996 but has since been stemmed.

Nevertheless, one analyst said that NEC, which is Japan's biggest chip maker, would be alone among the nation's major chip firms in turning a profit in semiconductor operations in the latest business year.
He added that NEC's chip profits are expected to expand because the stabilised prices are particularly beneficial for companies with a big chip-production system.
